sections.h2: What should you know before you sell a house in High Point, NC?
sections.html:
High Point is known as the Home Furnishings Capital of the World, and the city's tourism site says it hosts the High Point Market, a wholesale home furnishings trade show held each spring and fall. Sellers should expect that event to shape local traffic and short stays, and it helps explain why this city has a distinct rental market.

Most of the city lies in the southwest part of Guilford County. The city's financial report describes limits that reach into four counties, with about two percent of the area in Randolph, Davidson and Forsyth. That detail decides which tax office and register of deeds serve your parcel, so confirm the county on your deed before you call anyone.

  • List with an agent for the widest reach among buyers who work in the furniture industry or commute to Greensboro.
  • Sell on your own if you have a buyer lined up.
  • Use a cash purchase when you need to close fast or the house needs work.

sections.h2: Which county taxes a High Point house, and what changed in 2026?
sections.html:
Most High Point parcels are in Guilford County, which put new values into effect on January 1, 2026. Owners were notified in February 2026, the new values appear on the tax bill sent in July 2026, and the appeal deadline of May 15, 2026 at 5 p.m. has passed.

The county says it did the work in house with appraisers, using maps, aerial photography, street level images, sales analysis and field visits. The reappraisal covers residential, commercial and industrial land and structures, not cars or boats, which are valued each year.

The county's sample appeal evidence for homes is a useful checklist for any seller preparing a house:

  • Recent sales of comparable homes.
  • Evidence of physical problems.
  • A recent appraisal.
  • Square footage or property record card errors.
  • Outside factors such as flood zone.

The Guilford tax department has offices in Greensboro and High Point, and the appraisal line is 336-641-4814. A parcel in the Randolph, Davidson or Forsyth portion follows that county's schedule, so ask that county's assessor.

sections.h2: Does a Guilford County property tax appeal work the same way every year?
sections.html:
The state process is the same each year, though the dates differ in a reappraisal year. The county board of equalization and review first meets no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May.

Property tax appeal steps under North Carolina statutes
StepPrinted ruleSource
County board hearingRequest in writing or by appearance before the board adjournsG.S. 105-322
Board decisionMailed no later than 30 days after adjournmentG.S. 105-322
Property Tax CommissionWritten notice within 30 days after the board mailed its decisionG.S. 105-290

In a revaluation year the board finishes its work by December 1. A seller who intends to close soon can still ask the county to correct record errors, and a buyer may negotiate around an assessment under review.

sections.h2: Are there tax breaks that follow a High Point owner?
sections.html:
Yes, if the owner qualifies, and an owner may receive benefit from only one of three programs. A disabled veteran exclusion removes the first $45,000 of appraised value, and the state form says no age or income limit applies. It is filed with the county assessor, who must accept the form through June 1 before the tax year.

The elderly or disabled exclusion removes the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value, with an income limit of $38,800 for 2026. The circuit breaker caps tax at 4.0 percent of income for owners at or under the limit, and at 5.0 percent between the limit and 150 percent of it, after five years of owning and occupying the home. Deferred tax under that program is a lien and comes due on a transfer, so a seller using it should get a payoff from the county before closing.

sections.h2: What risks come with liens, land contracts or occupants on a High Point property?
sections.html:
Three problems come up often: tax liens, informal seller financing and people living in a house without a lease. Each has a statutory answer in North Carolina.

  • Tax lien: it attaches on the listing date, and the county can foreclose by an action like a mortgage foreclosure. A sale is by auction, and the owner can redeem before confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.
  • Contract for deed: under Chapter 47H, a buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day, and forfeiture needs a written notice with a cure date at least 30 days out.
  • Occupants: twenty years of possession under known and visible lines can give title against others, so do not ignore a long-time occupant of a vacant parcel.

A title search before listing finds these issues while there is time to fix them.

faqs.q: Which county do I deal with if I own a house in High Point?
faqs.a: Check the county on your deed. Most of High Point lies in Guilford County, and about two percent of the city's area extends into Randolph, Davidson and Forsyth counties, each with its own tax office and register of deeds.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal the 2026 Guilford value on my High Point home?
faqs.a: No. Guilford's appeal deadline was May 15, 2026 at 5 p.m. and the county lists the period as closed. Later appeals go to the county board of equalization and review, then the Property Tax Commission within 30 days of the board's mailed decision.

faqs.q: What is the income limit for the elderly or disabled exclusion?
faqs.a: The 2026 state form prints $38,800 for the 2026 tax year. The owner must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, and a resident of North Carolina.

faqs.q: Do I need to worry about a High Point Market effect on selling?
faqs.a: The market is a wholesale trade show held each spring and fall, according to the city's tourism site. Whether it changes the buyer pool for your street is a question for a local agent.

faqs.q: Can a tax lien force a sale of my High Point house?
faqs.a: Yes. The county can bring a foreclosure action on the lien, and the property is sold at auction. The owner may redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.
